title: Requesting persistent storage, with no claim about what it guarantees
outcome: `navigator.storage.persist()` is called once at boot, best-effort, covering the two loss causes the write-read-delete probe cannot see -- iOS ITP clearing storage after long inactivity and disk-pressure eviction -- neither of which throws anything for the probe to catch.
acceptanceCriteria: `navigator.storage.persist()` is called exactly once per app boot, guarded for browsers where `navigator.storage` or `persist` is absent.
Its resolved boolean is logged (or otherwise recorded for diagnostics) and nothing more.
Nothing is displayed to the user based on the result: it does not set `storageUnavailable`, does not change any of the five sync-status conditions, and adds no new UI.

The acceptance criteria and any accompanying comment are explicit that a `true` result means only that the request was accepted by the browser, not that data will survive eviction -- no durability guarantee is claimed anywhere in code or copy.
A rejected or unsupported call does not throw and does not block the rest of boot.
